reviews.comment: Lectures are clear. Quiz consisting of one or two proofs from a set of problems given or a lemma proven in class every week. Exams consists of the same.

I suck at proofs and if you do, I wouldn't recommend Bonito. 90% of the class is test and quizzes based. Homework or quiz every week. He's a decent professor but the way he lectures confuses me. I left this class until my final semester of college for a reason.

Don't be wary because of the grade distributions for this class with him. He is an incredibly reasonable person and in my opinion a pretty good professor. The exams are actually quite easy and all of the problems on the exams are given in the problem sets in class. There is actually not too much homework at all. Maybe about 2 hours every other wk.

He teaches very quickly, but if you pay attention and complete the assigned work (making sure to understand the material to build intuition), then it's a very reasonable class. Bonito is kind about questions and encourages them. His exams are all from a given set, which is large, but the tested proofs are not exceedingly difficult.

Very solid professor and a super nice guy. Either a quiz or a homework each week with quiz questions coming from a problem set. Exams were fair since all questions came from previous problem sets. If you participate in this course you will succeed.

Do not take the honors section of this class if you plan on ETAM-ing. Dr. Bonito is by far one of the most brilliant professors on campus, and should not be teaching a freshman 151 class. The lectures are entirely proof based, none of which appear on exams. The exams are not similar to the normal section common exams. Will probaly not ETAM now.

I like Prof Bonito as a person but try to avoid taking his class. I'm glad I took calc in high school, otherwise I would've been completely lost. He teaches from the textbook but is super heavy on proofs and his explanations did not make sense to me half the time, yet I had already taken calculus. I don't think he's taught many undergrads.

He's really sweet, makes funny jokes, and shows a genuine care for his students. He was easily accessible, would answer questions after class, go over problems after exams and review before exams as well. Loves soccer and made funny jokes about not spoiling the world cup game before he watched. He has a strong French accent but easy to understand.
